attribution.note: Zitron's own estimate, written in his own newsletter.

semantics.note: 'Reasonable to believe' is a hedge: it says the figure is plausible, not that it is true. The drafter rightly recorded the modality as 'likely'. Under policy, a hedged claim is not scored.

contract.note: The contract sets plain-reading support and contradiction conditions for a hedged estimate. Policy limits plain-reading scoring to firm language, so scoring this claim at all goes beyond what the speaker committed to.

evidence.note: Microsoft's FY2026 10-K property note has no separate CIP line. The $34.6B construction commitment is a different measure and neither confirms nor caps CIP.

reviews.rationale: The claim is a hedged estimate ('reasonable to believe'), which policy does not score. Even if it were scored, the packet has no Microsoft CIP figure and no reliable upper bound, so the evidence would leave it unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words, in his own newsletter.

semantics.note: 'Will eat their profits alive' is a firm, undated forecast. Dropping 'alive' softens the intensity slightly but does not change what the claim commits him to.

contract.note: Reading the claim as substantial depreciation-driven erosion of net income across the four named hyperscalers is fair and ordinary. With no deadline or threshold, the result depends on that reading.

evidence.note: Meta Q3 2026: D&A rose but net income rose too. Operating profit fell mainly because of a litigation charge. The quarter mostly predates the post. This is a company disclosure.
Alphabet Q3 2026: depreciation rose and net income fell, but the release attributes much of the fall to equity losses. Operating income grew. This is a company disclosure.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline, and the early-resolution rule is not met. Meta and Alphabet show higher depreciation without group-wide net-profit erosion caused by depreciation, and that quarter mostly predates the post. Under the contract, a period of strong profits does not disprove an undated forecast.

semantics.note: In context, 'everybody' means hyperscalers and neoclouds struggling to bring capacity online. The universal scope is kept. The earlier 'if' sentence is argument, not a condition on the claim.

contract.note: Reading it as material deployment difficulty across the class is fair and ordinary. Using Q2 2026 as the period is a reasonable default.

evidence.note: Microsoft's own statement that it is bringing capacity online faster. This is a company disclosure and can coexist with bottlenecks, so it does not refute the claim.
Alphabet's CFO describes an industry-wide supply-constrained environment, which reflects demand outpacing supply. It does not show deployment difficulty at every operator.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no operator-level record of planned versus actual deployments. It neither shows difficulty across the whole class nor documents an operator that proceeded without difficulty. Both items are company statements that point in opposite directions without settling the claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own argument, in his own newsletter.

semantics.note: The claim joins an observation ('barely any compute' coming online) to a causal claim (an illusory demand signal). The normalisation drops 'even when built by the largest firms' and the 'otherwise' qualifier, but the core claim is kept.

contract.note: Reading 'barely any' as negligible usable additions, judged across major providers, is fair and ordinary. Requiring causal evidence fits the claim.

evidence.note: Transcript of CoreWeave's Q2 2026 call: about 500 MW of active power added, which challenges 'barely any'. But it covers one provider, and power is only a proxy. It does not test market-wide compute or the causal claim about demand.

reviews.rationale: The only evidence is one provider's power addition. The contract says that challenges the claim but cannot settle it market-wide. There is no comparable cross-provider measure of usable compute, and no evidence separating slow supply from real demand.
